Seminar Title:

Interference-Aware Adaptive Data Rate Optimization for Dense LoRaWAN Networks Using Reinforcement Learning

Abstract:

LoRaWAN has emerged as a promising communication technology for large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) applications due to its long communication range, low power consumption, and suitability for battery-powered devices. However, achieving reliable and energy-efficient communication in dense and dynamic network environments remains challenging, as variations in link quality, interference, device density, and macro-diversity can significantly affect network performance. The conventional Adaptive Data Rate (ADR) mechanism primarily relies on link-quality history and predefined adaptation rules, limiting its ability to respond effectively to dynamically changing network conditions and to exploit reception diversity provided by multiple gateways. Therefore, intelligent and adaptive transmission parameter optimization is required to improve the of packet transmission and energy efficiency of LoRaWAN networks. In this research work, a lightweight reinforcement learning-based approach is proposed for adaptive data rate in LoRaWAN networks. The proposed mechanism jointly adapts the spreading factor (SF) and transmission power (TP) using observed link-quality conditions, energy consumption, and Co-SF interference rate, without relying on pre-collected training data. It is further proposed to study and model a spatiotemporal interference-based ADR scheme for multi-gateway LoRaWAN networks, where spatial interference variations and gateway macrodiversity are incorporated into adaptive SF and TP selection. Furthermore, the impact of realistic urban deployment environments is proposed to be investigated by considering building-aware propagation effects to evaluate the robustness and adaptability of ADR under diverse channel conditions. In addition, an application-aware ADR optimization framework is proposed for healthcare IoT applications, where transmission parameters are adapted according to application-specific reliability and energy requirements. The proposed approaches will be evaluated using NS-3-based simulations under varying network densities and different propagation conditions, followed by hardware-based experimental validation. The proposed approaches will be compared against existing ADR schemes using packet delivery ratio (PDR), energy consumption, interference, and related communication-performance metrics.
